subject: NimbleHealth - request for isolation dossier and VPC peering details
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@nimblehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: NimbleHealth Compliance <compliance@nimblehealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-02 16:15:00 -0400
Subject: Isolation dossier and VPC peering details for EU production

Hi Logan and Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security and infra teams reviewed the brief notes you shared and asked for a tighter packet to complete our procurement checklist. Specifically they need the following before we can complete the CAIQ review: 

- A single PDF that maps customer traffic flows for EU production workloads, showing private peering endpoints and where KV cache and model artifacts are hosted.
- Confirmation of KMS/HSM tenancy boundaries: do customer keys for EU customers reside in customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed keys? If Redwood manages keys, we need key separation proof and rotation window.
- SOC 2 control references for data localization and network isolation (control IDs or page refs from your SOC 2 summary).
- A CAIQ appendix that calls out private endpoint options and any gateway egress behavior for third-party monitoring services.

We are targeting an internal review on Monday; is it possible to get a packet by end of day Monday EU time? If not, please propose a realistic date.

Regards,
Sofia Ramos
Head of Security Programs
NimbleHealth
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-02 18:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Isolation dossier and VPC peering details for EU production

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the clear list. We can deliver an assembly pack that contains the flow diagram, our CAIQ answers with an appendix for private links, and a SOC 2 controls summary referencing the relevant sections. High level answers to your KMS questions:

- For EU production customers we offer two options:customer-managed KMS via customer-provisioned keys in the customer cloud project, or Redwood-managed keys that are partitioned by tenant and stored in an HSM-backed service with strict access controls.
- When customers select Redwood-managed keys we provide a key-ownership diagram and a rotation window of 90 days by default; rotation can be tightened in contract.

I attached a draft VPC connection diagram and the working CAIQ workbook. The SOC 2 summary is included as a one-page reference. These are drafts; Irene (cc) will add the final control refs.

Can Irene and Priyom confirm two items we expect to include in the packet: the exact NimbleHealth tenant ID and whether you want the packet to state explicit SLA-bound key rotation cadence or leave it as configurable?

Attachments: redwood_vpc_connection_diagram_v1.pdf, redwood_caIQ_response_2026.xlsx, soc2_controls_summary_redwood.pdf

Best,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales - Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-03 08:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: Isolation dossier and VPC peering details for EU production

Forwarding Logan's drafts. Two clarifying notes from Security: 

1) KMS model detail: If NimbleHealth wants Redwood-managed keys, we need to attach the HSM tenancy diagram (separate from the general VPC diagram) and a short nonce-based attestation statement for key separation. I will draft the attestation but need confirmation that HSM logs are retained 365 days for EU tenants.

2) Private peering specifics: please confirm whether the intended configuration is PrivateLink-style endpoints (no public egress) or a VPCPeering with restricted route tables. The CAIQ appendix must call out NAT and egress behavior explicitly.

Priyom, can you verify the peering config we used in the diagram and update the CAIQ workbook with the egress matrix? I'll add SOC 2 control IDs once I crosswalk the one-pager to our latest report.

Irene Choi
Staff Security Engineer, Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-03 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Isolation dossier and VPC peering details for EU production

I updated the diagram and CAIQ workbook as requested. Notes: 

- Peering: NimbleHealth requested PrivateLink endpoints. The diagram now shows a PrivateLink endpoint per region with no transit gateway egress. Route tables are locked down; egress to monitoring providers is via an explicit outbound proxy in customer VPC unless the customer grants a specific allow rule.
- Keys: For Redwood-managed keys we retain HSM logs 365 days for EU tenants; I added that attestation sentence to the SOC 2 one-pager and linked the HSM-tenancy diagram.
- Action items for packet finalization:
  - Irene: please add SOC 2 control IDs (I'm pointing to controls 12.3, 14.1 and 17.2 as candidates).
  - Logan/Marissa: confirm NimbleHealth tenant ID and whether they want a contract clause for 60-day rotation instead of default 90-day.

I uploaded the revised files to the shared compliance folder: https://redwood-inference.sharepoint.com/sites/Compliance/packets/NimbleHealth-2026

Attachments included in the folder: redwood_vpc_connection_diagram_v1.pdf, redwood_caIQ_response_2026.xlsx, soc2_controls_summary_redwood.pdf

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
